subject: general
question: 1 EB is equal to ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1024 PB**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• EB stands for Exabyte, which is a unit of digital information storage.
 
• 1 Exabyte (EB) is equal to 1024 Petabytes (PB).
 
• Petabyte (PB) is a unit of digital information storage equal to 1024 Terabytes (TB).
 
• Exabyte is often used to measure data storage capacity for large-scale data centers and cloud storage services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exabyte (EB)**

 
 
• An Exabyte (EB) is a unit of digital information storage equal to 10^18 bytes (1,000,000,000,000,000,000 bytes) or 1024 Petabytes (PB).
 
• EB is used to describe large data sets and is often utilized in the context of big data, data warehouses, and cloud storage.
 
• For example, it is estimated that all the words ever spoken by humans would take up about 5 Exabytes of storage.
 
 
 
• **Petabyte (PB)**
 
 
• A Petabyte (PB) is a unit of digital information storage equal to 10^15 bytes (1,000,000,000,000,000 bytes) or 1024 Terabytes (TB).
 
• PB is commonly used to measure the amount of data in large databases and data warehouses.
 
• For example, the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) generates about 15 Petabytes of data annually.
 
 
 
• **Terabyte (TB)**
 
 
• A Terabyte (TB) is a unit of digital information storage equal to 10^12 bytes (1,000,000,000,000 bytes) or 1024 Gigabytes (GB).
 
• TB is commonly used to measure the storage capacity of hard drives and other storage devices.
 
• For example, a modern laptop may have a storage capacity of 1 to 2 Terabytes.
 
 
 
• **Gigabyte (GB)**
 
 
• A Gigabyte (GB) is a unit of digital information storage equal to 10⁹ bytes (1,000,000,000 bytes) or 1024 Megabytes (MB).
 
• GB is commonly used to measure the size of files, such as videos, photos, and software applications.
 
• For example, a high-definition movie may take up about 4 to 5 Gigabytes of storage.
